claim: The OpenSAFELY-TPP dataset comprises 24 million patients, covering over 40% of England's population.
source: With the approval of NHS England, and drawing from a nationally representative OpenSAFELY-TPP dataset of 24 million patients (over 40% of the English population), we undertook a cohort study of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the dataset size and population coverage in the Methods section.

claim: There were 26,840 people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer from January 2015 to March 2023.
source: There were 26,840 people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer from January 2015 to March 2023.
evidence: This is a direct count from the study data presented in the Results section.

claim: The mean age at pancreatic cancer diagnosis was 72 years (±11 SD).

claim: 48% of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer were female.

claim: There was a reduction in surgical resections by 25–28% during the pandemic.
